papers.title: On the Structure of Stationary Solutions to McKean-Vlasov Equations with Applications to Noisy Transformers
papers.abstract: We study stationary solutions of McKean-Vlasov equations on the circle. We establish an exact equivalence between solutions of the stationary McKean-Vlasov equation and an infinite-dimensional quadratic system of equations over Fourier coefficients, allowing explicit characterization of stationary states in a sequence space rather than a function space. This framework provides a transparent description of local bifurcations, their periodicity and resonance structures, while accommodating singular potentials. We derive analytic expressions for the emergence, form and shape (supercritical, critical, subcritical or transcritical) of bifurcations involving possibly multiple Fourier modes and connect them with discontinuous phase transitions. We also characterize, under suitable assumptions, the detailed structure of the stationary bifurcating solutions through leading small-amplitude coefficients for arbitrarily many fixed Fourier modes. At the global level, we establish regularity and concavity properties of the free energy landscape, proving existence, compactness, and coexistence of globally minimizing stationary measures, and identifying discontinuous phase transitions with points of non-differentiability of the minimum free energy map. We apply the theory to the Noisy Mean-Field Transformer model, where we show how changing the inverse temperature $\beta$ affects the geometry of the infinitely many bifurcations from the uniform measure. We also discuss how increasing $\beta$ motivates the study of approximate multi-mode stationary profiles as candidates for a separate metastability analysis; persistence times require additional dynamical estimates. Moreover, we determine the exact threshold $\beta_0\simeq2.447$ separating continuous and discontinuous phase transitions in this model. The same threshold marks the change of the first bifurcation from supercritical to subcritical.

papers.title: A structure-preserving finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a fully discrete finite volume scheme for the time-fractional Allen-Cahn equation with nondegenerate state-dependent mobility. The scheme combines a standard two-point flux approximation of diffusion, the L1 approximation of the Caputo derivative on a uniform time grid, and a semiconvex splitting of the potential, and it discretizes the inverse mobility by a secant average multiplying the entire L1 derivative. The key estimate is a lower bound for the accumulated pairing of this weighted L1 derivative with the solution increments in terms of the accumulated L1 quadratic form. Using this lower bound, we derive a discrete energy estimate and the time regularity required for compactness. For twice continuously differentiable semiconvex potentials satisfying sign conditions outside $(-1,1)$ and initial data in $H^1(\Omega)$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, we prove existence of at least one fully discrete solution on every admissible finite volume mesh and every uniform time grid. Every such solution satisfies the maximum bound principle and a discrete energy bound relative to the initial energy, without a time-step restriction. In up to three space dimensions, under a mesh regularity condition with a constant independent of the mesh size, we prove that any sequence of fully discrete solutions has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\Omega\times(0,T))$ to a weak solution of the continuous problem as the mesh size and time step tend to zero. As a consequence, we obtain existence of a weak solution in one and two space dimensions, and in three dimensions whenever such meshes exist.

papers.title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.

papers.title: A Unified Space-Time Variational Framework for Wave Equations on Differential Forms
papers.abstract: We revisit a standard space--time variational formulation of the scalar wave equation in the setting of differential forms. For this, we use as spatial operator the nonnegative, self-adjoint (relative) \emph{Hodge--Laplacian} on a bounded Lipschitz domain. Its spectral decomposition reduces the wave problem in any form degree to the same family of scalar ordinary differential equations that underlies existing space-time analysis. We illustrate how this can be used to transfer results from the scalar wave equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions to other wave-type problems. In particular, we connect the framework to perfectly electrically conducting Maxwell problems.

papers.title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
papers.abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. While these suction samplers provide critical local data, they inherently capture only a fraction of the subsurface environment, leaving wide areas unmonitored. Motivated by this real-world monitoring procedure, we propose steady and time-dependent advection-diffusion-reaction models to simulate contaminant transport. Our main contribution is a generalized unique continuation result demonstrating that, under appropriate physical and mathematical assumptions, two concentration fields coinciding on a non-empty observation region must match throughout the entire space-time domain, even when originating from different source configurations. We investigate this problem from both theoretical and numerical perspectives, backing our mathematical uniqueness results with numerical simulations that validate the efficiency and practical utility of our approach. The theoretical proofs combine regularity properties away from source singularities with unique-continuation principles for parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, providing a robust framework for environmental risk assessment and site remediation.

papers.title: A hyperbolic nonlinear Schr\"odinger system in multiple spatial dimensions: structure, convergence, and numerical discretization
papers.abstract: We propose and study a first-order hyperbolic approximation of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation in $N$ spatial dimensions. This is an extension of the recently-proposed 1D hyperbolic NLS model. We study the structure and properties of the hyperbolic approximation and their relation to those of the original system. We show that the N-dimensional hyperbolic system exactly conserves analogs of the mass, energy, and momentum, and that it possesses stationary solutions that are closely related to those of NLS. The hyperbolic system is also shown to admit plane-wave solutions that share some stability properties with those of NLS, and that relaxation can shrink the focusing low-wavenumber modulational instability band as well as introduce a high-wavenumber instability band not present in NLS. We also show that solutions of the hyperbolic system converge to solutions of NLS in the relaxation limit. We present an adaptive-mesh finite volume discretization of the hyperbolic system and demonstrate its effectiveness in handling simulations, including those with geometric obstacles or non-periodic boundary conditions. The effectiveness of the numerical scheme is demonstrated through examples including a Bose-Einstein condensate, line soliton instability, and superflow past a cylinder.

papers.title: Derivation of the fourth-order DLSS equation with nonlinear mobility via chemical reactions
papers.abstract: We provide a derivation of the one-dimensional fourth-order DLSS equation based on an interpretation as a chemical reaction network. We consider the rate equation on the discretized circle for a process in which pairs of particles occupying the same site simultaneously jump to the two neighboring sites; the reverse process involves pairs of particles at adjacent sites simultaneously jumping back to the site located between them. Depending on the rates, in the vanishing-mesh-size limit we obtain either the classical DLSS equation or a variant with nonlinear mobility of power type. Via EDP convergence, we identify the limiting gradient structure to be driven by entropy with respect to a generalization of diffusive transport with nonlinear mobility. Interestingly, the DLSS equation with power-type mobility shares qualitative similarities with the fast diffusion and porous medium equation, since we find traveling wave solutions with algebraic tails or compactly supported polynomials, respectively.

papers.title: Partial $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $W^{2, VMO}$ regularity for nondifferentiable fully nonlinear elliptic equations and Isaacs equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the partial regularity of viscosity solutions to fully nonlinear elliptic equations of the form $F(D^2u, x) = f(x)$ in previously unexplored settings: (i) When $F$ is non-differentiable with respect to $D^2u$. (ii) When either $F$ or $f$ lacks Dini continuity in $x$. In the first scenario, we introduce a tangent operator property for $F$ such that, for a fixed point $x_0$ and a given matrix $M_0$, $F(M, x_0)$ is tangential to a convex or concave operator at $M_0$. We establish partial $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity for equations exhibiting this property. In the second scenario, we establish new partial $W^{2, \text{VMO}}$ regularity provided that the oscillation of $F$ in $x$ under the $L^n$-norm is of order $o(\log^{-1}(1/r))$. We address the Hausdorff dimensions of the singular sets of solutions for equations of the form $F(D^2u)=f(x)$ with data $f$ in $W^{1,n}$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the tangent operator property holds for various classes of equations, including nondifferentiable twisted elliptic equations, infimum of $C^1$ equations, semiconvex equations, and piecewise differentiable equations. Finally, we tackle the issue of smooth enveloping and obtain partial regularity of solutions for three subclasses of Isaacs equations.

papers.title: Modeling and Analysis of Cooling Induced Isotropic Nematic Transitions in Pharmaceutical Liquid Crystals
papers.abstract: This paper studies the phase transition from an isotropic to a nematic liquid crystal driven by controlled cooling, motivated by the manufacturing of next-generation pharmaceutical drugs. Using the non-isothermal Ericksen model for liquid crystals with a variable degree of orientation, we formulate the problem as a stiff, quasilinear system of parabolic partial differential equations. We establish a consistent thermodynamic framework, prove the well-posedness of the system, and conduct a rigorous asymptotic and numerical scaling analysis of the moving phase boundary in a cylindrical cell subjected to bottom-wall convective cooling. Our analysis identifies a critical sample thickness that separates two distinct physical regimes. Below this threshold, the transition follows the cooling dynamics and the material remains quasi-isothermal. Above the thickness threshold, bulk thermal diffusion governs the dynamics, imposing a dominant thermal delay characterized by a concave quadratic propagation front. These results demonstrate that scaling from laboratory characterization to industrial production fundamentally alters the spatial thermal history of the material, providing a predictive mathematical framework to optimize cooling protocols for kinetic arrest.

papers.title: Fourier analysis on a class of Schwartz spaces and applications
papers.abstract: The study of regularity and solvability of partial differential operators on non-compact manifolds requires the construction of adapted functional spaces. In this work we introduce $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$, the Schwartz space on the product of a homogeneous space $\mathfrak{M}$ and the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$. We characterize $\mathcal{S}(\mathfrak{M}\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ and its topological dual by employing discrete Fourier analysis in terms of eigenfunction expansions associated with a class of anisotropic elliptic operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We provide a characterization via partial Fourier coefficients and via full coefficients, that is, with respect to both components of $\mathfrak{M} \times \mathbb{R}^n$ simultaneously, which is achieved by studying the Fourier analysis on $\mathfrak{M}$. Our results provide new tools for the analysis of operators in this broader setting. As an application, we investigate the global existence and regularity of solutions for a class of partial differential equations on $\mathfrak{M}\times \mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Beyond the reduced Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation: Singular potential, global well-posedness, and micromagnetic limits
papers.abstract: We study the full nonlinear mean-field Landau--Lifshitz--Bloch equation in micromagnetics arising from Garanin's spin-polarisation model [D. Garanin. Fokker-Planck and Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch equations for classical ferromagnets. Phys. Rev. B, 55 (1997)] prior to the usual near-equilibrium reduction. The equation combines a singular inverse-Langevin potential with a mobility whose longitudinal component degenerates at saturation, together with exchange, anisotropy, and the nonlocal whole-space stray field. The natural state space is the closed unit ball $|m|\leq 1$. For any $H^1$ initial data satisfying $|m_0|\leq1$, including saturated data of infinite free energy, we construct global weak solutions and derive instantaneous separation from saturation $|m|=1$. This restores uniform parabolicity and yields the thermodynamic formulation and exact energy identity for positive times. We further establish a quantitative low-temperature limit to the Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation and prove convergence of global trajectories to a single equilibrium. A spectral Curie-type threshold characterises the stability of the paramagnetic state and yields exponential relaxation above the threshold. Finally, for uniformly separated data we prove strong well-posedness, including global strong solutions in one- and two-dimensional domains, and exponential stability of non-degenerate equilibria, with a small-data global theory in three dimensions.

papers.title: Metastability of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional Ginzburg--Landau model with pinning
papers.abstract: We study the persistence of the Meissner state in the three-dimensional magnetic Ginzburg--Landau model with a spatially dependent pinning term. Factoring out the equilibrium profile associated with the pinning term reduces the problem to the analysis of a weighted Ginzburg--Landau functional. In the extreme type-II regime, we construct locally minimizing vortexless configurations for applied fields extending far beyond the first critical field. We obtain quantitative estimates showing that these configurations remain close, up to gauge transformations, to a Meissner-type state determined by a weighted London problem. We also prove the uniqueness, up to gauge transformations, of the locally minimizing Meissner-type branch within a quantitatively controlled class of local minimizers. A central difficulty is to derive elliptic estimates that remain uniform in the Ginzburg--Landau parameter in the presence of the resulting spatially dependent weight. Under a small-BMO assumption on this weight, we obtain the required regularity and extend to the three-dimensional pinned setting the metastability picture previously established for the homogeneous model.

papers.title: Bilinear Strichartz Estimates and Linear Morawetz Estimates for Schr\"odinger Operators with Potentials
papers.abstract: In dimensions three and above, we establish bilinear Strichartz estimates for Schr\"odinger operators with potentials using perturbative arguments and Morawetz estimates. Our approach does not require smallness of the potential. As part of the analysis, we also establish endpoint versions of the bilinear Christ-Kiselev lemma.

papers.title: Some Remarks on the Asymptotic Behavior of Mean Field Games of Controls
papers.abstract: We analyze the asymptotic behavior of several mean field games of controls. First, in the time-dependent case, we examine the behavior of solutions to discounted mean field games of controls as the discount factor $\lambda$ tends to infinity. Next, we study three stationary models of mean field games of controls, finding that solutions to the first-order discounted problem and the second-order ergodic problem can be obtained from solutions to the second-order discounted problem by taking $\nu \to 0$ and $\lambda \to 0$, respectively. Finally, we investigate the long-time average behavior of solutions to the time-dependent system with no discount, finding that solutions converge to the solution to the second-order ergodic problem as $T \to \infty$.

papers.title: Ground States of a Coupled Fractional Schr\"{o}dinger System under a Total-Mass Constraint: Complete Classification and Concentration Behavior
papers.abstract: We consider a coupled fractional Schr\"{o}dinger system with trapping potentials under a total-mass constraint, in which both the intraspecies and the interspecies interactions are attractive. For every fractional order $s\in(0,1)$ and dimension $N\ge1$, we obtain a complete classification of the existence and non-existence of minimizers: minimizers exist if and only if both intraspecies coefficients lie below the single-component critical mass and the interspecies coupling coefficient lies below an explicit critical threshold $\beta^*$, and no minimizer exists otherwise. The threshold $\beta^*$ is characterized by means of an auxiliary intensity function, which yields a lower bound for the energy functional without invoking a new coupled Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. As the coupling coefficient approaches $\beta^*$, we analyze the concentration behavior. In the one-dimensional half-Laplacian case, the two components are shown to blow up at a common zero of the trapping potentials and, after rescaling, to converge to the same fractional ground-state profile, with the mass ratio determined explicitly by the intraspecies coefficients and the critical mass. For polynomial trapping potentials whose flattest common zero has order $q_0\in(0,1)$, the sharp blow-up rate is established, and both components concentrate simultaneously at the flattest common minimum.

papers.title: L2-contraction and Asymptotic Stability of Monotone Shock Waves for Cubic and Quartic KdV-Burgers Equations
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear stability of monotone traveling shock waves arising in the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation with a power-law flux, focusing on the cubic and quartic cases p=3 and p=4, respectively, in the presence of both dissipative and dispersive effects. Since shocks connecting distinct end states destroy the integrable structure of the equation, we introduce a slowly varying reference connection to establish global well-posedness for the Cauchy problem in an affine Sobolev space. A key ingredient in the stability analysis is to establish a new two-sided comparison estimate for the derivative of a monotone shock-wave profile. After a monotone coordinate transformation, this estimate allows the viscous dissipation to be compared with the natural vanishing weight arising in a shifted Poincare inequality. Together with an $L^\infty$ bootstrap controlling the higher-order relative-flux terms, this yields a global $L^2$-contraction property modulo a time-dependent shift for sufficiently small $H^1$ perturbations in the admissible parameter regimes. We obtain exponential decay of the shock profile and show asymptotic convergence to the shifted shock in $L^q(\R)$, $2<q\leq \infty$, with vanishing shift velocity.

papers.title: Weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates of a generalized Oseen evolution operator in exterior domains, with applications to the Navier-Stokes flow past a rigid body
papers.abstract: We consider a generalized Oseen evolution operator arising from time-dependent rigid motions in 3D exterior domains. Hishida and the present author established the regularity theory of the evolution operator by use of the $L^q$-$L^r$ smoothing estimates with a weight function $(1+|x|)^{\alpha}$. The objective of this paper is to develop the weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ estimates globally in time. These estimates are applied to the study of the large time behavior of the Navier-Stokes flow around a time-periodic solution in weighted spaces.

papers.title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
papers.abstract:
We study stable regular solutions of the variable-coefficient equation $-\operatorname{div}((A(x)
abla u\cdot
abla u)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u)=f(u)$ in $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, where $p>1$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove quantitative interior H"older estimates for $n<p+4p/(p-1)$ when $p\ge2$, and for $n<5p$ when $1<p<2$. We also obtain interior energy estimates and higher integrability of the gradient in every dimension. These estimates are given in terms of $\|u\|_{L^1(B_1)}$, with constants depending only on $n,p$, the ellipticity bounds, and a local $L^\infty$ bound for $DA$, but not on $f$ or higher derivatives of $A$. These results extend the corresponding interior estimates of Cabr'e, Miraglio, and Sanch'on for the $p$-Laplace equation to this variable-coefficient setting. The proof uses weighted Hessian estimates to control coefficient errors and a comparison between radial and full gradient energies.

papers.title: On the unconstrained Allen-Cahn system and its Cahn-Hilliard limit
papers.abstract: In [F.P. Duda et al., Meccanica, 2021] the new theory for constituent migration in solids with microstructure was developed. We consider the one-dimensional version of the basic system of this theory with generally non-zero kinetic modulus and the particular diffusivity of the "fast diffusion" type. We obtain exact traveling wave solutions for this system, and analyze several unconstraint and constraint limiting cases. We show that in unconstraint cases of Allen-Cahn type, i.e. for two independent variables, the system demonstrates broader set of possible regimes; in the constraint limit only CH-type process remains.

papers.title: Power Concavity and Log-Concavity for Large-Parameter Robin 2-Hessian Problems
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge3$, be a bounded uniformly convex $C^{3,\gamma}$ domain, where $0<\gamma<1$. We study the limit as the positive Robin parameter $\alpha\to\infty$. For the $2$-Hessian torsion problem, let $U$ be the admissible Dirichlet solution. For all sufficiently large $\alpha$, we obtain a unique admissible Robin solution $u_\alpha$ and establish the optimal-order estimate \[ \|u_\alpha-U\|_{C^{2,\gamma}(\overline\Omega)} \le C\alpha^{-1}. \] Moreover, $-\sqrt{-u_\alpha}$ has a uniform positive lower bound on its Hessian, and hence $\sqrt{-u_\alpha}$ is strictly concave. For the normalized eigenvalue problem, let $(\lambda_D,\varphi_D)$ be the normalized negative admissible Dirichlet eigenpair, and assume $\varphi_D\in C^{2,\gamma}(\overline\Omega)$. For all sufficiently large $\alpha$, there is a unique normalized negative admissible Robin eigenpair $(\lambda_\alpha,\varphi_\alpha)$, which satisfies \[ \|\varphi_\alpha-\varphi_D\|_{C^{2,\gamma}(\overline\Omega)} +|\lambda_\alpha-\lambda_D|\le C\alpha^{-1}. \] The Hessian of $-\log(-\varphi_\alpha)$ also has a uniform positive lower bound. The main analytic tool is a uniform H\"older estimate for linear Robin problems, with an $\alpha^{-1}$ gain for $C^{2,\gamma}$ boundary data. A normalized augmented inverse removes the scaling kernel in the eigenvalue problem. A Schur-complement argument combines the $C^2$ convergence with boundary geometry to prove convexity up to the boundary and anisotropic Hessian lower bounds at the scale ${\rm dist}(x,\partial\Omega)+\alpha^{-1}$. The convergence rate $O(\alpha^{-1})$ for the Robin solution functions is optimal even in $C^0$, as follows from their boundary conditions.

papers.title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators
papers.abstract: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle A\omega,\omega\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.

papers.title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
papers.abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.

papers.title: Decay Rate toward the Rarefaction Wave and the Viscous Contact Wave for Jin--Xin Relaxation Model
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the time-decay rates toward the rarefaction wave and the viscous contact wave for the one-dimensional Jin--Xin relaxation system under the $L^1$ integrability condition of the initial perturbation. In the case of a strictly convex flux, we employ a decomposition method to derive a logarithmic $L^1$ estimate related to a conjecture proposed by Liu\cite{liu2001lp}. Furthermore, a time-weighted $L^2$ method yields the optimal decay rate toward the rarefaction wave. Regarding the case where the flux is partially linearly degenerate, by employing a similar \(L^1\) estimate and time-weighted \(L^2\) method, along with a refined estimate of the nonlinear wave interactions, we obtain the corresponding decay rate toward the composite wave. The decay estimates are obtained without smallness assumptions on the initial perturbations or the wave strength.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with localized boundary data
papers.abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and localized boundary data $\psi(x')\phi(t)\mathbf e_j$, $1\le j\le n$, where $\psi$ is supported in the closed unit ball. A separation point is a boundary point outside $\operatorname{supp}\psi$ where a component takes both signs on positive-measure sets in every sufficiently small adjoining space-time neighborhood. By evaluating the spatial convolutions appearing in the solution formula of the Stokes system via confluent hypergeometric functions, we obtain explicit formulas for the first normal derivatives of tangential components, the second normal derivative of the normal component, and tangential pressure derivatives at the boundary. For normal data, suitable H\"{o}lder regularity and strict log-concavity of $\phi$ yield a unique separation point for each tangential component at every point of its coordinate axis outside the ball, and exactly two for the normal component at each sufficiently distant boundary point. We prove monotonicity and large-distance asymptotics of their temporal coordinates and quantitative temporal vanishing estimates for the normal derivatives. For tangential data in $n\ge3$, we prove the existence and uniqueness of separation points of tangential and normal components, including at fixed spatial points while $\phi$ is positive. We derive spatial asymptotics at large distance and time from data moments and, under a geometric condition, supporting faces of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$. We characterize tangential pressure-gradient signs for both tangential and normal data, locating favorable and adverse regions near the boundary. For radial $\psi$, additional assumptions yield existence, uniqueness, and asymptotics of pressure-gradient zeros and zero curves, including those governed by the zero of the Caputo half-derivative of $\phi$.

papers.title: Global classical solutions of the repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system
papers.abstract: Global classical existence for general large data in the three-dimensional repulsive relativistic Vlasov--Poisson system has long been an open problem. We give an affirmative answer: every nonnegative $C^1$ initial datum satisfying \[ f_0(x,p)+|\nabla_{x,p}f_0(x,p)|\lesssim\langle x\rangle^{-a}\langle p\rangle^{-b},\qquad a>1,\quad b>3, \] generates a unique global classical solution. No smallness or symmetry is assumed. The result covers finite and infinite mass and energy, including infinite kinetic energy density. The power thresholds are sharp for general pure-power bounds ensuring finite density and an absolutely convergent Coulomb field. The proof rests on two new mechanisms: local energy recovery for a population selected by energy growth, and a corrected moment--action closure based on nonnegative transverse interactions. The argument also yields global classical solutions of the nonrelativistic equation in the same initial class, allowing infinite mass with polynomial velocity tails of any order $b>3$.

papers.title: Ground state uniqueness and quantitative stability for the mass-critical Hartree equation
papers.abstract: We prove that the ground state of the mass-critical Hartree equation is unique up to phase rotations and translations and nondegenerate in every dimension $d\ge3$. This makes the recent conditional $L^2$ classification of minimal-mass blow-up and non-scattering solutions unconditional; we also give a direct $H^1$ proof of the finite-time blow-up classification. We further establish a global quadratic stability estimate for the sharp Hartree interpolation inequality. For the optimal stability constant, we rule out vanishing of minimizing sequences and describe their possible loss of compactness.

papers.title: Inverse source problem of variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates an inverse temporal source problem for a variable-exponent time-fractional diffusion equation with time-dependent diffusion coefficients. By the perturbation method, the model is equivalently transformed into a constant-order fractional diffusion equation with a convolution perturbation term. Existence, uniqueness, and energy estimates of strong and weak solutions to the forward problem are established, and for a separable source term the uniqueness and Lipschitz stability of the temporal source function are proved using local integral observations. A numerical reconstruction algorithm combining Tikhonov regularization with the conjugate gradient method is developed with a convergence error estimate, and numerical experiments verify its effectiveness and stability for different variable-exponent functions, noise levels and source functions. Since fractional advection--diffusion models describe the turbulent transport of airborne pollutants, the method is also applicable in atmospheric science for recovering the emission history of a pollution source from sparse measurements.

papers.title: Stability of least-energy solutions of the harmonic map flow from the plane into the 2-sphere
papers.abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of the least-energy harmonic map $W:\mathbb R^2\to S^2$ for the harmonic map flow under small, sufficiently decaying, non-symmetric perturbations. Solutions exist globally and are asymptotically described by a modulation of $W$ plus a remainder that converges to zero as $t\to\infty$. The modulation parameters associated with scaling, rotation, and translation remain close to their initial values and converge to finite limits. The proof relies on an inner-outer gluing decomposition and the analysis of a non-local equation governing the modulation parameters.

papers.title: On the classification of entire solutions to the Allen-Cahn equation in any dimension
papers.abstract: The mathematical content that follows dates from 9 March 2016. I began writing it in early December 2014, whilst I was visiting Scuola Normale Superiore in Pisa, Italy. I would like to thank Luigi Ambrosio, Andrea Malchiodi, Carlo Mantegazza e G\'erard Tronel who, between January 2015 and March 2016, read this version of the manuscript and some earlier drafts. Their feedback and constant support have been a source of encouragement. The manuscript has been at rest since March 2016. Neither its content nor its status will undergo changes in the future; it asks merely to be considered through the eyes of that moment. Paris, October 23, 2026, Alberto Farina

papers.title: Far-field Layers of Steady State for Viscous and Heat-conductive Gas
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing heat conductivity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions to the non-isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the exterior of a ball under an inflow boundary condition. A distinctive feature of this singular limit is the formation of a far-field layer whose transition region moves toward spatial infinity as the heat conductivity tends to zero. We establish the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions with the uniform estimates with respect to the heat conductivity and analyze the corresponding limiting problem. The limiting solution generally fails to attain the prescribed far-field density and temperature separately, although its pressure at infinity agrees with the prescribed far-field pressure. We show that this discrepancy gives rise to a far-field layer, derive its explicit representation, and identify its characteristic spatial scale. Finally, we prove that the stationary solution is uniformly approximated over the entire exterior domain by the superposition of the limiting solution and the far-field layer.
